summary: US-B3: Event builder — an organizer publishes a sellable event without curl
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** to author and publish an event and its performance from the back office, **so that** I never touch the catalog API by hand.

This is the tracer bullet for the epic's second COS. It covers the **single-event → performance → ticket type → publish** path end to end in the browser. Series/season/festival authoring is deliberately a later slice — this one proves the shape.

**In scope:** back-office screens to create an event, attach a typed dated slot (performance) to it, define a ticket type with a price, and publish the performance; readable validation and refusal handling; the published performance is visible on the storefront.

**What the three tickets before this one already did for you** (do not rebuild any of it):
- **TKT-190** — the session. `Astro.locals.staff` carries the principal; the organizer comes from
  there, never from `DEFAULT_ORGANIZER_ID`.
- **TKT-191** — `postCatalog()` already attaches the staff-write credential, so a write from a new
  page needs no credential plumbing. Catalog will refuse it if the plumbing is bypassed.
- **TKT-197** — every new page **must** be classified in `ROUTE_MATRIX`
  (`web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts`) or the build fails. Authoring is `admin`-only; the nav
  link must come from `canAccessRoute`, the same source the gate reads.

**Out of scope:** series, seasons, festivals, operating-day slots, seat-map assignment (TKT-105 already owns map authoring), pricing rules beyond a flat price, archive/close/reopen from the UI.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] From `/admin/`, a signed-in `admin` creates an event, adds a performance to it, adds a ticket type with a price, and publishes the performance — with no HTTP call issued outside the browser.
- [ ] The published performance is then visible on the storefront and can be put in a cart.
- [ ] A publish that the catalog refuses (ADR-018: a grouped member refusing its own publish, an archived slot) renders a readable message on the form — never a 500 and never a silent no-op.
- [ ] Invalid input re-renders the form with a field-level error and the operator's entered values intact.
- [ ] Money is entered and submitted as integer minor units + an ISO currency code; no float appears on the price path.
- [ ] Every new form posts a **relative** action and is verified by an actual submit against `make up`.
- [ ] Every new page is classified in `ROUTE_MATRIX` as `admin`-only, and a `box_office` or
      `finance` session pasting the URL is refused — proven by driving it, not by the link being
      absent (TKT-197 COS-5's rule: hiding a link is never the enforcement).
- [ ] The nav entry point to the builder is rendered from `canAccessRoute`, so the nav and the gate
      cannot disagree.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS + gateway smoke suite).
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary; OpenAPI regenerated and committed before the gate (ADR-009).
- UI story: the write forms are **submitted** against the real stack (`make up`), not just rendered — API smoke cannot see the SSR layer (TKT-105 learning).
- Read endpoints declare their ADR-004 TTL tier; auth/session responses are `no-store`.

governingAdrs.why: The gateway is the single public entry point and its route table IS the security boundary; /api/<svc>/internal/ is unreachable from the edge by construction. Anything this ticket adds to the edge must keep that construction true.

Contract-first: a new HTTP surface is authored in the service's openapi.yaml and the generated code committed BEFORE the gate runs — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.
Response drift fails closed: every status code the handler can emit must be declared, or the validator rejects the response at runtime.

The back-office is Astro SSR behind the gateway. `security.checkOrigin` is already false in web/backoffice/astro.config.mjs and form actions must be RELATIVE — an absolute action trips the check even same-origin.

Publish/archive are state-deriving transitions: they decide under a row lock and emit after commit, and a grouped member (festival day) refuses its own publish. The UI must surface that refusal as a readable error, not translate it into a 500.
A performance is a typed dated slot with attributes, not a bare date — the builder authors the typed shape the catalog already models.
Publishing emits performance.published, currently at schema 5 (TKT-183). The builder must not change the payload; if it would, that is a consumer-semantics bump, not a field addition.
Any list read the builder needs must be backed by an index to be genuinely scoped — copying a query shape that scales ships a no-op.

As amended twice: the back office holds a write-capable catalog credential (TKT-191) and the route matrix decides which staff member may drive it (TKT-197). A new authoring page inherits both — it needs no credential work, and it MUST be classified or the build fails.

reference.summary: Catalog write surface the builder drives: /events, /performances, /performances/{id}/publish, /ticket-types.
Existing back-office page + api client shape to extend (venue list, seat-map editor).
Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code; floats are banned on money paths.
The route matrix a new page must join, and canAccessRoute for the nav. A page under src/pages/ with no rule fails the enumeration test in both directions.

objective.note: Problem and why stated in the description; lineage to TKT-22's COS.

scope.note: In-scope and out-of-scope both enumerated on the ticket.

uncertainties.note: Named in the description's out-of-scope list; the remaining design choices are safely settleable in Planning without a mid-sprint redesign.

dependencies.note: blocked-by links wired; catalog/commerce/access endpoints this depends on are shipped and stable.

approach.note: Settled by TKT-190/191/197: session for the organizer, postCatalog for writes (credential already attached), ROUTE_MATRIX for the role gate. Planning wires an existing stack rather than choosing one.

first_slice.note: The ticket IS one vertical slice — schema/backend/UI/tests — demoable on its own.

success.note: COS are verifiable criteria plus the project quality gates.

context_memo.note: Baked at decomposition with governingAdrs resolved against docs/adr/ at HEAD 2026-08-03; every cited ADR file verified to exist.

# TKT-192 plan — Event builder

## Design summary

Build one admin-only page, `/admin/events/new` (NEW), using the established `_action` dispatch, post/redirect/get, and caught-error pattern from [venues/[id].astro](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/src/pages/venues/[id].astro:1).

The page advances through four forms:

1. Create event.
2. Create performance.
3. Create ticket type.
4. Publish performance.

No catalog contract, credential, event-payload, storefront, database, or infrastructure changes are needed.

All occurrences below of `/admin/events/new`, `events/new.astro`, `event-builder.ts`, `event-builder.test.ts`, `backoffice_event_builder_test.go`, the client wrappers `createEvent()`, `createPerformance()`, `createTicketType()`, `publishPerformance()`, the helper `parseBuilderSubmission()`, and the listed query/action names are **NEW**.

## 1. Page and route shape

One page:

- `web/backoffice/src/pages/events/new.astro` — **NEW**
- Astro route template: `/admin/events/new` — **NEW**
- One new `ROUTE_MATRIX` row:

```ts
{ template: '/admin/events/new', source: 'page', roles: ['admin'] }
```

The static `new` segment is supported by `isSupportedTemplate`; there is no mixed-segment routing.

The existing `/admin/` page gains a “Create event” entry point only when:

```ts
canAccessRoute(`${base}/events/new`, staff.role)
```

returns true. The link and middleware gate therefore continue to read the same matrix. `box_office` and `finance` see no link, while direct URL access still returns 403.

## 2. State across the four steps

Use query-string resource IDs on the same page:

- `event` — **NEW**
- `performance` — **NEW**
- `ticket_type` — **NEW**
- `published=1` — **NEW**, display-only completion marker

Flow:

```text
/admin/events/new
  → ?event=<event-id>
  → ?event=<event-id>&performance=<performance-id>
  → ?event=<event-id>&performance=<performance-id>&ticket_type=<ticket-type-id>
  → same IDs plus published=1
```

Each successful action uses `Astro.redirect(..., 303)`. The next GET renders completed-step summaries and only the next form. Query parameters carry identity, not editable domain data and never the organizer. Every create payload takes `organizer_id` from `Astro.locals.staff.organizerId`.

Every form omits `action`, matching the relative same-page submission used by [venues/[id].astro](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/src/pages/venues/[id].astro:1). A hidden `_action` selects:

- `create-event` — **NEW**
- `create-performance` — **NEW**
- `create-ticket-type` — **NEW**
- `publish-performance` — **NEW**

On failed submission there is no redirect. The current form’s raw strings are retained in server-render state and written back into `value`/selected attributes alongside field errors.

If the operator abandons midway:

- Already-created catalog resources remain drafts; there is no delete operation to roll them back.
- Retaining/bookmarking the URL allows continuation.
- Losing the URL means there is no draft-discovery/resume UI in this ticket.
- No cookie, local storage, new database state, or cleanup workflow is introduced.

The query IDs are not treated as authorization. The admin route is the staff control; catalog remains authoritative for existence, lifecycle, and organizer consistency. The path-only publish operation has no organizer argument at HEAD, so this ticket should not pretend to add tenant enforcement that its existing contract cannot express.

## 3. Localized strings

Both localized entities collect both supported locales:

| Form | Inputs | Catalog payload |
|---|---|---|
| Event | English name, French name | `name: { en, fr }` |
| Ticket type | English name, French name | `name: { en, fr }` |

Whitespace-only values fail locally with an error attached to the relevant input. The submitted raw values remain visible after failure.

Event description is omitted: it is optional and not needed by the ticket. This satisfies `SupportedLocales = ["en", "fr"]` for every required localized name, including the ticket type, which is validated by the same catalog helper as event names.

## 4. Performance and money

### Typed performance

The builder creates only `kind: "performance"` and supplies:

- `event_id`
- selected `venue_id`
- `starts_at`
- `timezone`
- `organizer_id` from the session

It does not expose festival or operating-day attributes, re-entry policy, or seat-map assignment.

To avoid treating the back-office server’s timezone as the venue timezone, `starts_at` is a text field requiring RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, for example `2026-09-18T19:30:00+02:00`. `timezone` is a separate IANA name such as `Europe/Paris`, checked with the platform’s timezone support before submission. Do not use an unqualified `datetime-local` value unless a correct IANA-zone-to-instant conversion is added.

### Integer money

The price form uses:

- Text input `amount`, labelled “Amount in minor units,” with `inputmode="numeric"` and a digits-only pattern.
- Text input `currency`, requiring exactly three uppercase ASCII letters.

Conversion path:

1. Preserve the submitted amount as a string.
2. Require `/^[0-9]+$/`.
3. Convert through `BigInt`.
4. Reject values above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.
5. Convert the validated integer to the generated OpenAPI `number` representation.
6. Send `{ amount, currency }`.

There is no `parseFloat`, decimal separator, multiplication by 100, division, rounding, exponent notation, or fractional intermediate.

## 5. Refusal and error path

Add four narrow wrappers in [api.ts](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts:1), all calling the existing private `postCatalog<T>()`:

- `createEvent()` — **NEW**
- `createPerformance()` — **NEW**
- `createTicketType()` — **NEW**
- `publishPerformance()` — **NEW**

They accept the session organizer explicitly where the contract requires it. They do not default to or reference `DEFAULT_ORGANIZER_ID`, and add no credential code: `postCatalog<T>()` already attaches the deputy credential.

The page catches `CatalogApiError` and renders its parsed `{error}` message inside the active form panel with `role="alert"`. Other exceptions receive a safe generic message. A refusal therefore produces an HTML 200 re-render, not an uncaught page 500 or redirect.

At minimum, the existing catalog messages surfaced unchanged are:

- Grouped member: `grouped festival day must be published/archived via its festival`
- Archived performance: `illegal performance lifecycle transition`
- Missing ticket type: `performance has no ticket type; create one before publishing`
- Existing 400/404 organizer, reference, timezone, and validation errors

No lifecycle decision is duplicated in the UI. Catalog still makes the transition decision described by ADR-018.

No catalog OpenAPI change is planned. All statuses already emitted by these handlers are declared. No generated file should change.

No domain-event code is touched. One nuance at HEAD: schema 5 is the highest current `performance.published` variant, but [events.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/services/catalog/internal/events/events.go:336) selects the schema from payload shape. This unseated, ungrouped GA performance continues to use the existing plain-GA variant; the builder must neither alter the payload nor force schema 5.

## 6. Verification by COS

| COS | Vitest | Smoke against real stack | Manual browser |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Client payloads contain session-supplied organizer and correct endpoint/body | Sign in as admin and submit all four `/admin/events/new` forms through `postForm`; assert each 303 and resulting IDs | Complete the entire builder with DevTools open; browser sends only admin-page form posts, never hand-issued catalog calls |
| 2 | Ticket payload pins exact localized names and integer price | Create through the UI forms, GET the unique storefront detail and list, assert names/price, then obtain a hold through commerce using the created ticket type | Open the storefront detail and click the existing `HoldPicker` Reserve action |
| 3 | `publishPerformance()` throws `CatalogApiError` carrying status/message | Prepare grouped and archived fixtures through test setup, submit the builder’s publish form, assert HTML 200 plus exact readable alert and no redirect | Normal publish submits the same real browser form; refusal rendering is covered deterministically by smoke |
| 4 | Table-driven validation tests assert field key and unchanged raw value for every step | Submit at least missing French name and malformed minor units; assert field error, retained value, and no redirect | Exercise representative invalid event and price submissions |
| 5 | Assert `"4550"` becomes integer `4550`; reject `45.50`, exponent notation, signs, overflow, and lowercase/invalid currency | Storefront renders the submitted integer amount as localized money | Inspect the authoring field and resulting storefront price |
| 6 | Authorization/page assertions pin the intended relative form shape where practical | `postForm` sends the gateway Origin and successfully traverses every new form | Required: submit every new form against `make up`; inspect requests and redirects |
| 7 | `canAccessRoute` admits only admin; enumeration sees exactly one new page and row | Extend the existing `signInAs` URL-paste test for both `box_office` and `finance`; both receive 403 while admin receives 200 | Paste `/admin/events/new` under each non-admin session |
| 8 | Assert the root-page route check uses `/admin/events/new` and the matrix decision | Root page contains the link for admin and omits it for both other roles | Confirm the same behavior in each session |

The repository has no cart abstraction. Its current sellable storefront action is `HoldPicker` → Reserve → `POST /api/commerce/reservations`; COS-2 should prove that real seam rather than invent a second cart model.

The smoke test should use a unique event detail URL to avoid a stale minutes-tier page-cache false negative and boundedly retry reservation creation until the publication consumer has provisioned inventory.

## 7. TDD order

1. **Authorization first**
   - Add assertions for `/admin/events/new`.
   - Red assertion: `canAccessRoute(..., "admin")` is currently false, and the known-route assertion lacks the page.
   - Add the matrix row and page skeleton.

2. **Validation and value preservation**
   - Add `event-builder.test.ts` (**NEW**) against `parseBuilderSubmission()` (**NEW**).
   - Red assertions: missing `fr`, whitespace names, bad RFC 3339/timezone, missing venue, decimal amount, overflow, and invalid currency return field errors while retaining the exact submitted strings.
   - Implement the standard-library-only parser.

3. **Catalog client wrappers**
   - Extend `api.test.ts`.
   - Red assertions: the four exports do not exist; once declared, tests require exact paths, request bodies, explicit organizer IDs, integer money, credential attachment through the shared helper, and parsed refusal messages.
   - Implement the wrappers without credential changes.

4. **Full form workflow**
   - Add `backoffice_event_builder_test.go` (**NEW**) before the page behavior.
   - Red assertion: admin GET is 404 or missing `_action="create-event"`.
   - Implement each form one at a time, keeping all four submissions in one end-to-end test.

5. **Invalid submission**
   - Red assertion: invalid input currently lacks a field error and retained `value`.
   - Wire parser errors into the SSR form state.

6. **Publication refusals**
   - Red assertion: grouped/archived publish POST does not yet render the catalog message on the builder.
   - Catch `CatalogApiError` and keep the publish panel rendered.

7. **Storefront and sellability**
   - Red assertion: the UI-created fixture does not yet appear on the storefront and cannot reserve.
   - Complete publish PRG, storefront assertions, and bounded reservation attempt.

8. **Navigation and role URL refusal**
   - Red assertion: admin root lacks the entry point.
   - Add the `canAccessRoute`-derived link and extend the real-stack URL-paste matrix for both refused roles.

## 8. Files

- `web/backoffice/src/pages/events/new.astro` — **NEW**; the single four-step SSR builder.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/event-builder.ts` — **NEW**; pure form parsing, validation, and exact integer-money conversion.
- [web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts:1) — add the four thin catalog wrappers; no credential plumbing.
- [web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/src/lib/authorization.ts:35) — add one admin-only route row.
- [web/backoffice/src/pages/index.astro](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/src/pages/index.astro:1) — add the matrix-derived navigation entry.
- `web/backoffice/test/event-builder.test.ts` — **NEW**; field validation, retained values, and money-path tests.
- [web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/test/api.test.ts:1) — endpoint, payload, credential-reuse, and refusal tests.
- [web/backoffice/test/authorization.test.ts](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/web/backoffice/test/authorization.test.ts:1) — route enumeration and role assertions.
- `smoke/backoffice_event_builder_test.go` — **NEW**; browser-shaped form workflow, invalid form, refusals, storefront rendering, and reservation seam.
- [smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.tkt-184-tighten-review-findings/smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go:350) — extend the existing role URL-paste/nav test to the event builder.

Explicitly unchanged:

- `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` and generated API files: no contract or regeneration change.
- `services/catalog/internal/events/events.go`: no event payload/schema change.
- `compose.yaml`: no change.
- Catalog migrations: none.
- CI configuration: no change.
- Storefront source: no change; existing event pages and `HoldPicker` consume the published catalog data.

## 9. Definition of Done

- One admin-only page completes all four operations through browser form submissions.
- Both event and ticket-type names include non-empty `en` and `fr`.
- Every failed form has an associated field error and retains submitted values.
- Money remains an integer-minor-unit path end to end.
- Grouped and archived publish refusals render exact readable catalog messages.
- Storefront renders the UI-created event and its existing Reserve action successfully creates a hold.
- Admin sees the entry point; `box_office` and `finance` neither see it nor reach the pasted URL.
- No new dependency, OpenAPI change, generated drift, migration, Compose change, or CI change.
- Run `pnpm --filter backoffice build` before the gate because Vitest does not typecheck.
- Run `make deps` first on a clean clone.
- Run `make check` as the sole command in its shell call and inspect the complete log for `Error [0-9]+`, `FAIL`, or `drifted`.
- Complete the real `make up` browser submissions and role-paste checks after automated tests.

## Risks

- **Abandoned drafts:** partial flows leave catalog drafts with no discovery UI. Accepted for this scope; cleanup/resume authoring would be a separate product decision.
- **Start-time UX:** RFC 3339 with an explicit offset is less friendly than a local picker, but is unambiguous and avoids shipping incorrect DST/timezone conversion.
- **Query-state tampering:** IDs are browser-controlled. Catalog still validates references and organizer relationships on creates; the existing publish contract remains path-only. Do not claim stronger tenant isolation.
- **Eventual inventory provisioning:** publication is synchronous to JetStream, but inventory consumption is asynchronous. Smoke reservation needs a bounded retry rather than a timing-sensitive immediate assertion.
- **Storefront cache:** use a unique event/detail cache key and avoid pre-fetching it before publish.
- **Error interaction:** test the complete sequence after composing validation, PRG, query state, and refusal handling; isolated green tests are insufficient.

## Size estimate

Estimated change: **720–790 lines** including tests.

That stays just under the split threshold if the page remains one server-rendered file, styling stays minimal, validation is table-driven, and smoke reuses `signInAs`, `postForm`, `created`, and `postJSON`. I would not split the ticket at plan time: the four operations form one dependency chain and COS-2/3 only become meaningful after publication. If implementation exceeds roughly 800 lines, stop and re-estimate rather than silently expanding into resume/discovery, richer datetime controls, reusable wizard components, or new storefront/cart behavior.
